title: How grand we are this morning!
html_source:
Bloom goes from being hurt by John Henry Menton, to hoping that Mr Cunningham will put Menton in his place, to suggesting that Menton might regret his treatment of Bloom on further reflection, to closing with this thought.

At one layer, this is Bloom sarcastically mocking Menton’s overinflated sense of his own importance, or at least Menton’s sense that he is superior to Bloom.

At another layer, it is Joyce’s poetic exclamation about the entirety of these characters and this work.
